title: Standalone Cascading: Effects, Modifiers & Unified Shader Options

blocks.content: Engineering notebook from `docs/STANDALONE_CASCADING_EFFECTS_AND_MODIFIERS.md`. This archive preserves the project’s original rationale, equations, performance reports and illustrative code. Historical paths, API names, claims and sketches can differ from the current engine. For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/STANDALONE_CASCADING_EFFECTS_AND_MODIFIERS.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/STANDALONE_CASCADING_EFFECTS_AND_MODIFIERS.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.

This document specifies the architectural design and developer API for **cascading shader effects** (`PathEffect`, `FillEffect`) and **geometric path modifiers** (`PathModifier`, `PathModifierPipeline`) in the Retiam WebGPU Engine.

It explains how these systems operate as **independent, standalone mathematical and shader graph processors** without requiring any [`Path`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Path.ts) or [`Entity`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Entity.ts) instance, and how they seamlessly integrate into [`PathOptions`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Path.ts#L28-L45) with clean, non-redundant configuration.
In Retiam, geometry modification and fragment shader synthesis are strictly decoupled from entity orchestration:

items: **PathModifiers** are pure geometric operators that take input curve contours (`PathContours`) and return transformed output contours (`PathContours`).
**PathEffects and FillEffects** are pure WGSL shader stage generators that accumulate algorithmic visual rules and compile them into optimized WebGPU fragment shader functions.

**The [`Path`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Path.ts) Entity** is merely a consumer/orchestrator of these two independent pipelines, connecting modified geometry to GPU staging buffers and binding compiled shaders to the render pass.

blocks.text: Both stroke shaders ([`PathEffect`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/material/PathEffect.ts)) and fill shaders ([`FillEffect`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/material/FillEffect.ts)) can be constructed, chained, combined, and compiled to raw WGSL code with zero entity dependencies.

When multiple effects are cascaded, Retiam's shader compiler wraps each stage into an isolated WebGPU function (`_pe_stage_0`, `_pe_stage_1`, ...) and executes them in strict sequence, feeding the resulting color `c` of one stage into the next:
Every builder method on [`PathEffect`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/material/PathEffect.ts) returns the instance (`this`), mutating its internal stage sequence:

When effects are created modularly or passed from different sources, [`PathEffect.combine()`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/material/PathEffect.ts#L390-L401) merges them into a single continuous chain:
The same model applies to 2D interior fills:
Geometric modifiers operate on pure mathematical vector curves (`PathContours`), where each contour is an array of parametric `Curve` segments (`Line`, `CubicBezier`, `QuadBezier`).

Because every [`PathModifier`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/modifiers/PathModifier.ts) exposes `apply(contours: PathContours): PathContours`, you can compose them as pure mathematical transforms:

For production use outside of an entity, [`PathModifierPipeline`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/modifiers/PathModifierPipeline.ts) provides dirty-checking, memoization, and automated execution order:
4. Integration with Entities (Path, Rect, Circle, Ellipse, SVG)

When rendering with Retiam's WebGPU primitives, you configure stroke shaders, fill shaders, and modifiers directly via [`PathOptions`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Path.ts#L28-L45).
To avoid API pollution and naming conflicts, Retiam standardizes on 3 clear properties:

When options are passed to [`SVG`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/composites/svg/SVG.ts), they are automatically cascaded to all parsed child paths and primitives:

On any instantiated [`Path`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Path.ts) (or subclass like `Rect`, `Circle`), the following methods manage the live cascade:
